newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle up on firmer live, but pare gains.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle up on firmer live, but pare gains.

text.p: A firmer tone to cash cattle kept CME live cattle futures supported but prices ended under best levels as weakness in beef clipped gains at the close, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.575 to 0.100 cent higher with April up 0.375 at 65.650 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.475 to 0.150 with March up 0.225 at 67.575 cents.

Increased packer demand for fed cattle and sales at $62 per cwt continued to support live cattle futures. However, weakness in boxed beef at noon caused some late selling that pared best levels, traders said.

Buy stops were hit on the early advance which followed the reports of increased packer interest for slaughter cattle. Packers appeared short bought and raised their bids to obtain needed slaughter numbers, they said
Lind-Waldock bought February while LFG sold. RBH purchased April while Refco, Cargill Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man sold. R.J. O'Brien bought February and April early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses spread long April 64 puts/short 68 calls on a one-for-two basis. They also sold the April 64/67 straddle. Volatility was steady in April, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of live cattle and pared best levels late. Feeders rose early on local short covering and buy stops despite a lower CME feeder cattle index. The market appeared somewhat oversold after setting 5-week lows Monday, traders said.
Shorts continued to point to expectations of increased feeder marketings.

Although feeder marketings at Oklahoma City were less than expected on Monday, increased numbers are projected. There will be more feeders next week and if not then they will come the following week. The feeders are still out there and have to come to market sooner or later, they said.

But longs now look for feeders to be kept on grazing longer because commercials were able to place hedges in back months before futures prices tumbled. They will keep them on grass longer and deliver them later, one trader said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.87 at $69.42 per cwt.
